result_semantic_payload.summary:
The device owner's account is the owner's own chat account (file:/chat/account_main.log), which contains three self-descriptive messages. The role the owner asserts for themselves is "chief operator / money handler": they claim to be the one who actually runs the operation and that all the money passes through them ("总操盘，钱都过我手"), that the rest of the group only recruits people while they settle the accounts ("群里那帮人只管拉人，账我来平"), and they note that after tightened risk controls they paused for a few days. This is a boastful self-description by the speaker, not an attestation by a third party.

The README (file:/README.txt) is explicit about the evidentiary ceiling: a self-descriptive boast in a chat is proof only that the statement was made, and is not independent proof of the role; no corroborating identity or operational data links the owner to the ledger flows (file:/ledger/flows.txt, which lists USDT movements between wallet-A/B/C with no account attribution).

Therefore the strongest assertion strength for the owner's actual role is HYPOTHESIS. At FACT strength only the following can be stated: the owner's account made these role claims, and the ledger file contains these flows. The claim that the owner actually was the chief operator / money handler through whom the funds passed cannot be stated as FACT or even as a well-grounded INFERENCE, because the only source is the subject's own uncorroborated assertion and the ledger carries no attribution to the account.

Important scope caveat: the delegated scope was 'windows', but the task context reports no platform scenario and no registered source scopes, and no Windows-derived artifacts (event logs, registry, prefetch/amcache, account or logon data) exist in the evidence set. The role analysis therefore rests entirely on the chat log, README, and ledger text files.

claim_candidates.text: The device owner's own chat account contains a self-description in which the owner claims the role of chief operator of the scheme and money handler: they state that they run the operation and that all money passes through them, and that the other group members only recruit people while the owner settles the accounts.
The owner's account additionally states that after risk controls tightened they stopped for a few days, consistent with a self-described active operational role rather than a passive one.

A self-descriptive boast in a chat is proof only that the statement was made, not independent proof of the role; per the case README no corroborating identity or operational data links the device owner to the ledger flows.

The owner's actual role as chief operator / money handler can be stated only at HYPOTHESIS strength; it cannot be asserted as FACT or as a well-grounded INFERENCE, because the sole support is the subject's own uncorroborated assertion and the ledger flows carry no attribution to the owner's account.
limitations: The ceiling is set by the absence of independent corroboration, not by any contradictory evidence.

The chat log carries no cryptographic or platform-level authentication of the speaker, so even the attribution of the messages to the device owner rests on the case README's statement that the chat log is the owner's own account.
